evidence:
Assembled source joins iPhone data-flow fc55bc7e9 with staging 37e1c2c8f. Native build floor remains 1 and the reviewed contract hash is unchanged. Notification context, reply metadata and nullable delivery columns are additive; ordinary tap routes, server_url and preference shapes remain compatible. Dispatch retains saved context and staging current-task eligibility checks. A no-op migration joins notification_message_context and merge_home_staging_compaction. Native Ticket/navigation decoding retains staging recap freshness fields. Compact conversation previews now decode optional sender attribution and owner-message preview from existing server status facts, only under current authority, while retaining local unsent delivery precedence and excluding transcript admission.

Verification: native unit suite completed 216 tests with 1 expected skip and zero failures. Supplemental diagnostic collection was interrupted after tests completed. The final host suite passed 176 tests, including the remote-refusal regression; 17 system host cases also passed. Fifteen local UI scenarios passed across recorded source pins. The final unsigned Release Simulator build passed on 953fae9ed. These results cover local source and fixture contracts. Full Linux server confirmation remains a separate gate. Exact pins, reruns and diagnostic limits are in the Ticket evidence. An oldest supported signed build, physical iPhone behavior, Apple notification delivery and account distribution remain unproved. No production deployment or next phone build is claimed by this compatibility review.

Recovery admission review: changes to the startup server and deploy interruption coordinator alter retry timing and update admission. They do not change native routes, request headers, response schemas, build policy, or recovery prompt contents. The supported build floor remains 1. The recovery integration suite and focused recovery tests passed. The iOS build gate unit and integration tests passed on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior; native reads, actions, conversation output, reconnect, unsupported-build handling, and draft retention on the oldest signed build remain release checks.

Worker cleanup review after merge with staging 037dc21386910b351541ba16fc7f5141115cd2f0: Reviewed Worker cgroup cleanup changes against staging 7a835e0b32b55be8da78ad2eeeaeb747ddcc4415. Changed backend files cover Linux launch, process ownership, cleanup and executor service serialization. No HTTP route, request field, response field, event shape, database schema, iOS source or build policy changes. CleanupResult retains complete/reason/scope with the same types; scope text now describes cgroup custody. ConversationAPI.interruptConversation still POSTs /api/conversation/conversations/{id}/interrupt and accepts the existing 204 response from conversation/api.py. Unsupported Linux cleanup retains the existing uncertainty path and fence, without a new native enum or decoding requirement. MINIMUM_SUPPORTED_BUILD remains 1. Verification: 25 existing Python compatibility/build-gate/stop-recovery tests passed; prior focused supervision/backend suite passed 37 tests with zero skips and executor installation passed five. This source review establishes unchanged native wire contracts; physical iPhone behavior and signed-device delivery were not tested on this Linux host. Native CI checks run on the refreshed PR. Recovery admission changes only retry scheduling and workspace admission, while Worker cleanup controls process retirement. Their sources do not overlap and neither changes native wire contracts.

Mac credential handover review: the change moves the original Mac's handover closure to the executor update-report route and makes the Mac executor ask for its credential at each start. It changes only executor routes and the Mac executor client. The iPhone app reads /api/executor/health alone, and that route, its response schema, native request headers, and build policy are unchanged. The supported build floor remains 1. The credential handover unit tests, the full unit suite, and the executor integration tests passed on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior.

Publish repair review: the only backend change splits one string literal in conversation/backend_state.py across two lines for the line-length lint rule. The model refusal text is identical, and no route, field, schema, event shape or build policy changes. The supported build floor remains 1. The check script and the ruff and mypy checks pass on Linux. This source review does not prove signed-device behavior. The Mac credential handover change (t_xwkw9uw5) moves the old-authority closure from the executor update-report route to a new credentialed POST /api/executor/credential/handover/close, used only by Mac and Linux executor runtimes. The iPhone app reads only /api/executor/health (checked by grep over ios/**/*.swift), whose shape is unchanged, so native builds from 1 remain compatible.

Proposal send-back compatibility review: the native Review outbox already sends the inspected expected_proposal_revision in protected decision operations and reuses the operation ID and frozen body. The server keeps the existing receipt contract and replay; a stale or resolved proposal produces an ordinary refused receipt, while writer contention produces HTTP 503 with no receipt and leaves the same operation eligible for recovery. The legacy direct native returnReview also supplies expected_proposal_revision. No iOS build-floor change is needed. The real HTTP busy-writer test verifies 503, no receipt, and successful retry with the same operation ID. Native source inspection confirms the outbox treats 5xx as uncertain and checks for a receipt before another attempt. iOS build-gate and decision-operation unit checks were run on Linux. The oldest signed build, TestFlight delivery, reconnect, physical device and signed-device behavior were not tested; they remain release checks.
